target_customer: Defense, aerospace and critical infrastructure organizations needing electronics supply chain assurance
problem: Compromised or counterfeit hardware is hard to detect; the company uses side channel and echo response signals to detect attacks on physical devices.
business_model: Enterprise and government hardware testing product and contracts

founders.name: Sebastian Fischmeister
founders.background_notes: YC page: 20+ years in embedded systems safety and security.

founders.name: Carlos Moreno
founders.background_notes: YC page: electronics engineer focused on embedded systems security.

technical_complexity.rationale: Physics based detection with AI on hardware signals needs lab equipment and patented methods.

defensibility.rationale: Patents from the University of Waterloo and specialized hardware know how.

market_need_then: The company won an In-Q-Tel and SVB innovation award in 2022 and landed Canadian defense contracts by 2021 per Velocity Incubator.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche defense buyer brand; no press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Palitronica spun out of University of Waterloo research and sold to defense buyers. It closed a BDC led Series A in 2026 and was selected by Bell Textron for cyber assurance on the MV-75, signalling slow but real enterprise traction in a long sales cycle market.
notes: Series A amount undisclosed. Velocity article is dated August 2026 while another outlet dates it September 2026. Seed and grant amounts from CB Insights ($230K) and FundedIQ ($50K) conflict and are unverified. No dated competitor from 2022 found; aggregator rival lists were recent and conflicting, so the list is empty.
